tracks.title: Clearance Rack Two-Step

tracks.title: Lutut Bunyi Krek

tracks.title: Kucing Tuan Rumah
tracks.genre: Malay rockabilly (1950s rock and roll revival)
tracks.subject: a tenant in Petaling Jaya who gets fifty ringgit off his rent each month for bathing his landlady's huge, furious Persian cat called Datuk every Saturday

tracks.genre: KL rempit club (Malay gabber-breakcore with kompang)

tracks.title: 佮松仔冤家 Kah Tshîng-á Uan-ke

tracks.title: 鏡面的字 Kiànn-bīn ê Jī

tracks.genre: Thai melodic hip-hop ballad with live band

tracks.subject: a young man in a Thủ Đức apartment assembling a flat-pack wardrobe over a whole Sunday, finishing with seven screws left over, and the wardrobe standing anyway

tracks.title: Con Vẹt Bấm Còi
tracks.subject: a parrot in a Gò Vấp alley in Sài Gòn that learns to copy its owner's scooter horn, so every neighbour keeps stepping aside for a motorbike that never comes

tracks.title: Cuốn Từ Điển Mượn
tracks.subject: a man returning, fifteen years late, the English dictionary he borrowed from his high-school teacher in Quy Nhơn, with her pencil notes still in the margins

tracks.subject: two flatmates who cannot sleep making red bean soup at two in the morning in a tiny Sham Shui Po kitchen, dancing around the pot while it simmers

tracks.mood: tender, warm and a little shy

tracks.title: 倉鼠越獄

tracks.subject: a woman whose boyfriend's model railway slowly takes over their dining table track by track, until they eat dinner on the sofa and the little train delivers the soy sauce

tracks.title: Burung Kakatua Pak Udin

tracks.title: Seragam Jangan Dicuci
tracks.subject: a girl on her last day of SMA whose white uniform shirt is covered in friends' marker signatures, hiding it in her cupboard so her mother will not put it in the wash

tracks.title: ベランダ・プール

tracks.subject: a man who rides the long transfer escalator up with his girlfriend every evening only to say goodbye at the top and ride straight back down alone

tracks.title: 벽 색깔 샘플
tracks.subject: a tenant who tapes six paint-colour samples on her rental wall and lives with them for a week while waiting for the landlord to reply

tracks.title: 새 안경
tracks.subject: walking out of the optician with a new prescription and noticing the individual leaves on a street tree for the first time in years

tracks.title: 영수증이 지워졌어요
tracks.subject: a man trying to get a warranty repair on a stick vacuum when the thermal-paper receipt in his drawer has faded completely blank

tracks.title: 일요일 어항 청소
tracks.subject: a man's Sunday ritual of cleaning the tank of the goldfish he won at a school fair eleven years ago, which now outweighs every other fish in the shop

tracks.title: Cermin Mata Pertama
tracks.genre: Malay bossa-samba jazz-club pop (Dendang Raya lane)
tracks.subject: a woman taking her boyfriend for his first pair of glasses at an optical shop in Bangsar, and the moment he puts them on and finally sees her face clearly

tracks.title: Harga Rak Lain
tracks.genre: Malay chart pop-rap duet (Garam & Madu lane)
tracks.subject: a customer and a hypermarket cashier arguing in rhyme when a pack of biscuits scans at RM12.90 but the shelf tag says RM8.90, while the queue behind them takes sides

tracks.title: Abang Din Paip
tracks.genre: Malay country-folk with harmonica (1980s Kembara lane)
tracks.subject: a plumber called Abang Din who comes to fix a dripping kitchen tap, finds three more leaks, and stays for teh o while the pipes are off

tracks.title: Ikan Laga Bilik Sewa
tracks.genre: Malay lo-fi hip-hop (chill beat with sung hook)
tracks.subject: a young man in a rented room in Shah Alam who changes his one betta fish's water every Sunday night and talks to it about his week

tracks.title: Cha-Cha Kolam Awam
tracks.subject: a thirty-five-year-old man taking swimming lessons at a public pool on Saturday mornings in the same class as six-year-olds, who cheer the day he finally floats

tracks.title: 洗喙齒的恰恰 Sé Tshuì-khí ê Tshiah-tshiah
tracks.mood: nervous, then playful and swinging, a dance-floor comedy in a dental chair
tracks.subject: a grown man terrified of a teeth cleaning whose hygienist hums a salsa under her mask and counts the scaling in clave so he keeps his mouth open to the beat

tracks.title: 十一冬的工具箱 Tsa̍p-it Tang ê Kang-kū-siunn
tracks.mood: driving, warm and a little sheepish, a road song with a big open chorus
tracks.subject: a man driving a red metal toolbox down to Changhua to return it to the coworker who lent it eleven years ago, every wrench still wrapped in the newspaper he packed it in

tracks.title: 新目鏡 Sin Ba̍k-kiànn
tracks.mood: tender, slow-burning and smiling, a real love duet between two old people
tracks.subject: an old couple at a neighbourhood optician, where she spends an hour choosing his new frames and he says he only agrees because the first face he sees through them is hers

tracks.title: 金魚仔大王 Kim-hî-á Tāi-ông
tracks.mood: bouncy, mock-grand and silly, a stomping comedy
tracks.subject: a man who buys his single fat goldfish ever more expensive imported pellets, which it spits out every time, until it gobbles the cheapest flakes from the corner shop

tracks.title: 發票白去矣 Huat-phiò Pe̍h--khì--ah
tracks.mood: frantic, wry and dancing, a shop-counter farce that ends friendly
tracks.subject: a woman taking a broken electric fan back to the appliance shop with a receipt so faded it is blank paper, she and the young clerk tilting it under the lamp to read the date

tracks.title: แว่นแรก (First Glasses)
tracks.genre: Isan molam sing (fast electric phin dance)
tracks.subject: a Khon Kaen rice-truck driver at his first eye test who reads the letter chart wrong with total confidence and then sees the price of the frames

tracks.title: สีที่สิบห้า (The Fifteenth Colour)
tracks.genre: Thai Bakery Music-era alternative pop revival
tracks.mood: warm, unhurried and quietly in love
tracks.subject: a couple painting fifteen sample squares of almost-identical off-white on the wall of their first rented room and choosing by lamplight at midnight

tracks.title: ใบเสร็จจาง (Faded Receipt)
tracks.subject: trying to return a pair of too-short trousers at a department store refund counter with a thermal receipt that has faded to blank paper

tracks.title: เหมียวใต้ม้านั่ง (Cat Under the Bench)
tracks.mood: gentle, fond and a little comic
tracks.subject: a woman at a Nonthaburi vet clinic coaxing her ginger cat out from under the waiting-room bench for its yearly vaccine while a large dog watches politely

tracks.title: หนังสือที่ยืมครู (The Teacher's Book)
tracks.subject: a man in his forties posting back a dog-eared Thai poetry book he borrowed from his primary-school teacher thirty years ago, with a short letter tucked at page forty

tracks.title: Màu Cửa Nhà Tôi
tracks.subject: a woman in Đà Lạt arguing with an old house painter over the colour of her front door, rejecting eleven sample patches on the wall until he quietly mixes the exact faded blue of the door she grew up with

tracks.title: Cái Quạt Bằng Bàn Tay
tracks.mood: petty, cheeky and laughing at himself
tracks.subject: a Hà Nội student who orders a cheap standing fan online during a sale and receives a fan the size of his palm, then spends a week arguing with the shop's chat for a refund and ends up keeping it on his desk

tracks.title: Bé Mập Ăn Kiêng
tracks.subject: a Biên Hòa woman whose round corgi is put on a strict diet by the vet, and who keeps slipping it pieces of bánh tráng under the table until the next weigh-in shows it gained half a kilo

tracks.title: Lịch Hẹn Ba Tháng
tracks.subject: a young man in Vĩnh Long who books a teeth cleaning every three months only to see the dental nurse, until she writes her phone number on the back of his appointment card

tracks.title: Lớp Bơi Tám Tuổi
tracks.subject: a thirty-year-old Hà Nội office worker who signs up for summer swimming lessons at a public pool and ends up in a class of eight-year-olds who teach him to blow bubbles

tracks.title: 貼紙樽
tracks.subject: a woman staying over at her boyfriend's flat who writes masking-tape labels for every unmarked jar in his kitchen, and he keeps them all even the wrong ones

tracks.title: 張單冇咗字
tracks.mood: frantic, cheeky, laughing at bad luck
tracks.subject: a man trying to return a broken desk fan to a Wan Chai electrical shop with a thermal-paper receipt that has faded completely blank

tracks.title: 浮唔起
tracks.subject: a forty-two-year-old woman in an adult beginners' swimming class at a Kowloon public pool who cannot float without her kickboard, until the coach quietly lets go

tracks.title: 金魚第三年
tracks.subject: a ten-dollar goldfish won for a girlfriend's niece that nobody wanted, now three years old in its third bigger tank in a Tai Kok Tsui flat

tracks.title: 三十二隻白
tracks.subject: a couple choosing a wall colour for their first 300-square-foot flat from thirty-two almost identical white paint chips at a Mong Kok hardware shop

tracks.title: 四十八種白
tracks.subject: a man in an empty rental flat holding up forty-eight paint swatches that are all slightly different whites while his girlfriend chooses, and he paints the wall in the one she calls 'morning milk'

tracks.title: 五塊錢的郵票
tracks.subject: a young man who buys a 1980 monkey-year-looking stamp at a Sunday flea market for five yuan, sure it is worth a fortune, and the old appraiser with a magnifier tells him it is worth exactly five yuan

tracks.title: 穿拖鞋的凌晨一點
tracks.subject: a woman who locks herself out in pyjamas and slippers while taking out the rubbish at 1 a.m., and the locksmith who arrives in a dinosaur-print jacket and opens the door in eleven seconds

tracks.title: 牙線週
tracks.subject: a man who has not flossed in a year and flosses ostentatiously for the seven days before his dental check-up, and the hygienist who sees his bleeding gums and says 'only started this week, huh'

tracks.title: 嗶不過的閘門
tracks.subject: a commuter whose transit card fails at the same metro ticket gate every morning, and the station attendant who starts waiting by that gate to wave him through, until he buys a new card and walks to her window anyway

tracks.title: No Receipt, No Problem
tracks.mood: cocky, petty and laughing at himself
tracks.subject: a Newark guy trying to return a pair of white trainers to a shoe store with no receipt, arguing with the teenage clerk over the scuff on the left toe, and walking out with store credit for exactly one pair of socks

tracks.title: Sunday Collars
tracks.subject: a woman teaching her new boyfriend to iron his own work shirts on a Sunday night: steam hissing, collars first, and the one blue shirt he scorches, which she keeps as a nightshirt

tracks.title: It Comes Back Black
tracks.subject: a London renter at war with a black mould patch on her bathroom ceiling that returns every three weeks no matter how much bleach she uses, until the landlord finally sends someone to fix the extractor fan

tracks.title: Shell on Seven Mile
tracks.subject: a Detroit man whose forty-year-old pet tortoise Big Ron escapes the backyard and is found three blocks away at the car wash on Seven Mile, where the whole crew starts chanting his name

tracks.title: Garage Line
tracks.subject: a retired bus mechanic in Fresno whose HO-scale model railway grows out of the spare room, across the hallway and through a hole in the garage wall, until his wife's car is parked on the street and she asks for a station named after her

tracks.title: Setengah Cokelat Setengah Kacang
tracks.subject: a young couple in Bandung at midnight with money for only one martabak manis, arguing chocolate-cheese against peanut at the cart on Dago until they order it half and half and end up feeding each other the other side

tracks.title: Member Januari
tracks.genre: East Java sound horeg battle-bass DJ
tracks.subject: a man in Surabaya who signs up at a shophouse gym on the second of January, goes exactly once, and keeps paying the monthly auto-debit all year while the receptionist still waves at him by name

tracks.title: Botol Teh Mbak Sri
tracks.subject: a young man in Ngawi who drinks bottled tea every day to fill a sack for the kampung waste bank, just to stand at the Sunday scale while Mbak Sri, who runs it, weighs plastic and writes balances in her ledger without looking up

tracks.title: Jenderal di Atas Atap
tracks.genre: Indonesian late-80s slow rock power ballad
tracks.subject: a man in Tanah Abang keeping six chickens on his rooftop whose rooster Jenderal crows from the water tank at four every morning and wakes the whole gang, until the bubur seller thanks him for never being late

tracks.title: Saldo Kurang
tracks.subject: a young office worker at Tebet KRL station who keeps his commuter card balance low on purpose because the woman behind him at the ticket gate always taps him through with hers and lets him pay her back with a bottle of iced tea

tracks.title: ネジが一本足りない
tracks.mood: flustered, cocky and laughing at himself
tracks.subject: a man assembling a flat-pack wardrobe alone on a Saturday, discovering one screw is missing so a door hangs crooked, while a wooden dowel is somehow left over and fits no hole

tracks.title: 最後に来たのはいつですか
tracks.subject: a man who has dodged the dentist for three years, finally walks in with a cracked filling, and freezes when the hygienist asks when he last came

tracks.title: ツナマヨふたつ
tracks.subject: two regulars at the same konbini at 11pm who keep reaching for the last tuna-mayo onigiri, until one night he buys two and hands her one, and they eat side by side at the guardrail outside

tracks.title: ボックスシーツのたたみかた
tracks.subject: a twenty-something living alone who finds a children's-TV-style how-to song in his head while trying, and failing, to fold a fitted bedsheet with elastic corners on a Sunday afternoon

tracks.title: ビート板は二枚まで
tracks.subject: a forty-two-year-old office worker in a ward-pool adult beginners' swimming class on Thursday nights, the oldest of six, finally letting go of his second kickboard and making twenty-five metres of crawl while the seventy-year-old woman in the next lane cheers

tracks.title: 왼발부터
tracks.mood: shy, giggly and slowly falling in step
tracks.subject: a couple in their thirties taking a Tuesday-night beginners' social tango class at the ward community centre, stepping on each other's feet for weeks, counting under their breath, until one night they get through a whole song without looking down

tracks.title: 오픈 기념
tracks.subject: a college student working a one-day part-time job inside a giant smiling SIM-card mascot costume outside a phone shop's grand opening in July, dancing every time the MC shouts 'music!', unable to see more than a mesh slit, high-fiving kids and a confused delivery rider

tracks.title: 싱크대 밑에
tracks.subject: a young man who adopts a grey shelter cat that hides under his kitchen sink for nine days; he sits on the kitchen floor every evening reading the instructions on ramen packets aloud until on the ninth night the cat walks out and sits on his foot

tracks.title: 열 번만 더
tracks.subject: a man rehabbing a sprained ankle at a neighbourhood physiotherapy clinic, doing calf raises and resistance-band pulls while his strict physiotherapist counts out loud and keeps saying 'ten more' every time he reaches ten

tracks.title: 몬스테라
tracks.subject: a man in a one-room studio whose small monstera bought at a flower market grows a new split leaf every week until it blocks the window, covers the TV and claims half his single bed, and he keeps rearranging his life around it instead of pruning

tracks.title: Manual Bahasa Cina
tracks.genre: Malay Afropop (Afrobeats pop with Malay melody)
tracks.subject: friends assembling a big trampoline for the kids at a Hari Raya open house, the instruction manual printed only in Chinese

tracks.title: Teh Tarik Bergambar
tracks.mood: warm, shy and quietly in love
tracks.subject: a teh tarik puller at an Ipoh kopitiam who makes the same drink for one woman every morning and finally draws something in the foam

tracks.title: Baju Yang Sama
tracks.genre: Malay cinematic folk-rock with French-pop melody (Noh Salleh lane)
tracks.subject: a tailor in Kampung Baru who has to let out the same customer's baju Melayu every week before Raya because he keeps eating at buka puasa bazaars

tracks.title: Latihan Kebakaran
tracks.subject: an office's monthly fire drill in a KL tower, everyone walking down 23 floors to the assembly point still carrying their nasi lemak

tracks.title: Empat Puluh Kunci
tracks.genre: Brunei-Malay traditional pop fusion (Aziz Harun lane)
tracks.subject: a tenant locked out in the evening and an elderly landlord arriving with a ring of forty unlabelled keys, trying every one on the grille door while they chat

tracks.title: 媽祖宮的榕仔 Má-tsóo-king ê Tshîng-á
tracks.mood: fond, gently swaggering and unhurried, a mid-tempo singalong about a morning routine
tracks.subject: an old man who sweeps the fallen banyan leaves in a Mazu temple courtyard every dawn and chats to the tree, and after one morning off sick finds a mountain of leaves waiting, which he takes as the tree missing him

tracks.title: 熱水器歹去矣 Jia̍t-tsuí-khì Pháinn--khì-ah
tracks.mood: shivering and indignant, then laughing, a street-corner complaint you can dance to
tracks.subject: a man whose gas water heater dies mid-shower on the coldest night of the Taipei winter, who boils pot after pot of water to rinse the shampoo out, only for the repairman to find next morning that the gas tank was simply empty

tracks.title: 牆仔欲漆啥物色 Tshiûnn-á Beh Tshat Siánn-mi̍h Sik
tracks.mood: warm, easy and smitten, a slow-dance love song
tracks.subject: a young couple choosing a paint colour for their first rented flat in Tainan, twelve sample patches daubed on the wall, arguing mint green against milk white at sunset, then painting half each until their rollers meet in the middle and she writes his name in the corner before painting over it

tracks.title: 鵝仔來矣 Gô-á Lâi--ah
tracks.mood: frantic, silly and bouncy, a chase-scene dance track
tracks.subject: a fierce goose nicknamed the Sergeant at a Yilan farm guesthouse that charges every tour group off the bus, stealing an auntie's sun hat, until one quiet teenager crouches down and buys peace with a sweet-potato cake

tracks.title: 歪膏的頷巾 Uai-ko ê Ām-kin
tracks.mood: wry, tender and warm, a clumsy gift told with a grin
tracks.subject: a man secretly knitting his wife a scarf at midnight from online video tutorials, pausing and rewinding every stitch, who runs out of grey yarn and knits a green row through the middle, and on New Year's Eve she wears it and offers him the longer end

tracks.title: ซ้อมมวยหลังเลิกงาน (After-Work Muay Thai)
tracks.subject: office workers in an after-work Muay Thai fitness class (a workout, not a fight), the trainer shouting for twenty more kicks while the accountant and the IT guy collapse on the mat, and everyone limping to work the next morning

tracks.title: ต้อนเป็ดข้ามถนน (Ducks Across the Road)
tracks.subject: a boy herding his family's two hundred ducks across a provincial highway at dusk with a bamboo pole and a red bag, while a ten-wheel truck and a pickup wait, and counting them all again on the far bank

tracks.title: รอน้ำพร้อม (Waiting for the Water)
tracks.subject: a couple who set up their first fish tank in a Nonthaburi condo and must wait six weeks for the water to cycle before buying a single betta, testing the water strip together every night

tracks.title: หมีตัวโตขึ้นวิน (Big Bear on the Bike Taxi)
tracks.subject: a woman who wins a giant pink teddy bear at a temple-fair ring toss and has to ride home on a motorcycle taxi with the bear squeezed between her and the driver, its ears covering his eyes

tracks.title: จีบนิ้วหน้ากระจก (Jeeb in the Mirror)
tracks.subject: a schoolgirl practising Thai classical dance hand curves (jeeb) in the wardrobe mirror every night for her school's Wai Khru day, her little brother copying her from the doorway with tangled fingers

tracks.title: Ly Thứ Tư
tracks.subject: four students cramming for a finals exam at a Sài Gòn café until two in the morning, ordering a fourth round of cà phê sữa đá while nobody has turned past page twelve

tracks.title: Băng Cát-Xét Duy Nhất
tracks.subject: a man fixing his late-90s National radio cassette player on the porch with a screwdriver and a pencil, and it only ever plays the one cassette left inside it, a worn Chế Linh tape

tracks.title: Cà Phê Trứng Bảy Giờ
tracks.subject: a Sài Gòn guy living in Hà Nội who whisks egg coffee every morning before work, failing for weeks, until he finally gets the thick foam his girlfriend loves from the café on Hàng Gai

tracks.title: Mảnh Ghép Cuối
tracks.subject: a woman spending a month of evenings on a 2000-piece Hạ Long Bay jigsaw on her living-room floor, finding the last piece missing, and cutting a stand-in from the box lid and painting it with a child's watercolours

tracks.title: Đứng Bên Phải Nha
tracks.subject: two friends riding the new Bến Thành - Suối Tiên metro escalators in its first months, one always standing on the left and blocking the people walking up, until the whole platform starts chanting at him

tracks.title: 張大口
tracks.mood: cheeky, flustered and laughing at himself
tracks.subject: a man at a dental scaling whose hygienist keeps asking him chatty questions while his mouth is propped open, so every answer comes out as 'ah' and she guesses wrong each time

tracks.title: 排到天光
tracks.subject: a man queuing at 6am outside a famous Hong Kong bakery for the fresh egg tarts his sleeping girlfriend wants, befriending an old regular with a stool, a woman doing her make-up and a paid queue-sitter

tracks.title: 同一盞燈
tracks.subject: two strangers who each bought the same old brass desk lamp at a Sham Shui Po flea-market stall meet when both come back for the one matching shade, and agree to share it

tracks.title: 皮鞋上獅子山
tracks.subject: a man who loses a bet to his friend and must hike up Lion Rock in brand-new leather office shoes, blistering, slipping and overtaken by grannies, then walking down barefoot

tracks.title: 一定係二
tracks.subject: a woman getting her first pair of glasses at thirty-one after an optician's 'one or two' lens test, walking out to find bus-stop signs, single tree leaves, and her partner waving from across the crossing suddenly sharp

tracks.title: 一個釘孔三百塊
tracks.subject: a young tenant moving out of a Taipei rental whose landlord walks the walls with a torch charging NT$300 for every nail hole, until he digs up his move-in photos proving three of the holes were already there

tracks.title: 你幫我挑的鏡框
tracks.subject: a very short-sighted man whose girlfriend picks his new frames at an optician by putting pair after pair on his face, and who, wearing the new lenses three days later, sees for the first time that she has more freckles on her left cheek

tracks.title: 九十九朵送錯樓
tracks.mood: frantic, cheeky and out of breath
tracks.subject: a florist's delivery boy who carries a 99-rose bouquet to floor 21 instead of floor 12, and has to talk it back off the receptionist who has already put it in a water bucket and photographed it for her mum, trading her a bunch of baby's breath to get it

tracks.title: 標籤寫三十九
tracks.subject: a shopper who finds the yellow shelf tag on a pack of toilet paper says 39 but the till rings 49, marches the cashier back to the shelf, makes the manager rip the tag down with his price gun, and an old man behind him quietly brings his own pack over too

tracks.title: 又胖了零點八
tracks.subject: a young woman whose shiba inu Xiaomi has gained 0.8 kg on the vet's scale because her grandmother secretly feeds it sweet potato, who starts extra evening walks past the roast sweet-potato cart, and at the recheck the dog is 300 g lighter while she has gained a kilo

tracks.title: One Waffle Each
tracks.subject: a British tourist at a Vienna hotel breakfast buffet who sets her alarm for six fifty-five every morning of the holiday to beat a German family to the only flip-over waffle iron, and on the last day finds the dad has left her the batter jug and a waffle already turning

tracks.title: Coach Twelve, Seat Sixty-One
tracks.subject: two strangers stuck for four hours on a Eurostar halted in a field outside Lille split the one tin of sardines, a squashed baguette and a clementine she had packed, swap numbers on the back of a ticket, and a year later book the same train, coach and seats on purpose, bringing two tins this time

tracks.title: Rocks on the Windowsill
tracks.subject: a woman whose boyfriend spends every weekend splitting shale in a disused Yorkshire quarry and fills her flat with ammonites on the windowsills, a trilobite in the butter dish and a hammer in the dishwasher, and she lists it all while not quite asking him to stop

tracks.title: Shake That Tree, Darlene
tracks.subject: an old Texas couple bringing in their pecan harvest in November with a tree shaker borrowed from the co-op for one afternoon only, the husband clamping the trunk while his wife drives the sweeper, nuts bouncing off the truck roof, both racing the co-op man who is coming at four to take the shaker back

tracks.title: Ride-On Through Bolton
tracks.subject: a council grounds worker in Bolton who mows the roundabouts and grass verges on a ride-on mower every summer, waves at the same bus driver at the same roundabout each morning, and spares one patch of wild orchids on the ring road verge that she tapes off with her own bunting

tracks.title: Lewat Harmoni
tracks.subject: a Jakarta commuter on TransJakarta who teaches the woman standing beside him how to transfer at Harmoni from the Blok M line to the Kalideres line, every morning for two weeks, until one day they both stay on the bus past Harmoni on purpose

tracks.title: Pesanan Kopi Lantai Tujuh
tracks.subject: a first-job intern on the seventh floor of a Jakarta office whose only task for three weeks is photocopying, until his supervisor finally trusts him to take and place the whole office's afternoon coffee order

tracks.title: Kelas Memanjat
tracks.subject: a keeper at an orangutan rehabilitation centre in East Kalimantan who spends every morning of forest school coaxing one orphaned young orangutan off her back and onto a liana, counting the metres it climbs before it slides down to her again

tracks.title: Beo Pian
tracks.subject: a Banjarmasin man whose talking myna was meant to learn a pantun for the bird show, but only ever learned his wife's voice calling him home from the riverside coffee stall, and now shouts it at him in front of his friends

tracks.title: Huruf Nenek
tracks.subject: a young man in Makassar learning the Bugis lontara script letter by letter from a primary-school workbook so he can read the folded letters his grandmother sent him while he worked in a Malaysian palm-oil plantation, which he kept for six years without ever reading

tracks.title: トング係
tracks.mood: flustered, eager and finally triumphant, a workplace comedy you can dance to
tracks.subject: a new hire at her first welcome party (歓迎会) at a yakiniku restaurant, handed the tongs by her section chief and put in charge of grilling for the whole table of eight, juggling who wants their meat rare, the burning tare and the chief's order of tongue first

tracks.title: こたつで千ピース
tracks.mood: hyperactive, nerdy and stubbornly proud, a grandpa's personal-best comedy
tracks.subject: a retired salaryman alone at the kotatsu over one winter weekend, timing himself on a stopwatch to finish the 1000-piece Mount Fuji jigsaw his grandson did in nine hours at New Year, sorting edge pieces into a biscuit tin and losing an hour to a sky made of nothing but blue

tracks.title: ハウスの朝
tracks.subject: a young couple who grow strawberries in Moka, Tochigi, picking tochiaika in the greenhouse at 5:30 on January mornings; he packs the boxes so she can pick at her own pace, and they split a can of hot oshiruko on the way back from the farm stand

tracks.title: 開かねえ
tracks.subject: a young man in Asahikawa at six in the morning at minus twenty-five whose car door handle and lock are frozen solid before work, scraping ice with a point card and warming the key with a lighter, until he gets in through the passenger door

tracks.title: 挟まれたもみじ
tracks.subject: a ward library staffer in November who keeps finding a pressed maple leaf inside different returned books each week, is not allowed to check the borrowing records to find out who, and one morning tucks a ginkgo leaf into the book as a reply

tracks.title: 곗돈 장부
tracks.subject: the narrator keeps the shared money book and the cash envelope for four school friends saving 50,000 won each a month for their first trip abroad together (Fukuoka), while one friend, Minjae, keeps 'borrowing' from it, until the narrator opens the envelope and finds Minjae has paid it all back with interest and a note saying to go get passport photos

tracks.title: 오백 원 저금병
tracks.subject: a girl who drops every 500-won coin into a narrow-necked drink bottle from January on to buy her best friend a birthday present, then finds the coins won't come back out through the neck, fishes for three hours with chopsticks and a hairpin, and ends up tying a ribbon on the whole bottle

tracks.title: 그늘막 점프
tracks.mood: sweaty, cheeky, dancing through the heat
tracks.subject: a man in Daegu during a 38-degree August heatwave who walks to a first date by hopping from one shade parasol at the crosswalks to the next, timing each dash to the walk signal, and arrives with his shirt soaked anyway

tracks.title: 칠 층까지 다시 칠해 주세요
tracks.subject: a young delivery rider who relies every evening on the floor numbers painted on the landings of an old walk-up apartment block, and the block's elderly caretaker (경비 아저씨) who repaints the faded numbers one landing per evening with a tape measure, finishing the seventh floor on the evening of the first snow

tracks.title: 스티커 붙였다고
tracks.subject: a man who buys a large-waste disposal sticker at the community centre for his old single mattress, gets the size category wrong, and watches the mattress sit untouched in the alley for two weeks with a pink 'wrong sticker' slip taped to it

tracks.title: Mesin Ais Lalu
tracks.subject: the driver of the ice resurfacing machine at a shopping-mall ice rink in Kuala Lumpur who clears the skaters off every two hours and crawls the machine round the rink at walking pace while forty teenagers wait at the gate

tracks.title: Bajet Atas Tisu
tracks.genre: bright piano-soul pop with brass (Tulus lane)
tracks.subject: a young man on his first payslip who sits at a kopitiam and budgets every ringgit on a paper napkin so he can take his girlfriend to the Italian restaurant in Bangsar she always pointed at through the glass

tracks.title: Tarik Tali Tin
tracks.subject: a Kelantan paddy farmer and his wife at harvest, taking turns all day in the bamboo hut at the edge of their plot pulling the long string of rattling tin cans to scare the burung pipit off the ripening grain, him pretending he is not tired while she brings the kopi in a tin can

tracks.title: Tali Lanyard Pejabat
tracks.subject: a young man alone in his newly rented room in Shah Alam whose curtain rod falls down every night with a crash; on the third night he gives up on the screws, ties the curtain back with his office lanyard and sleeps facing the orange streetlight outside the window

tracks.title: Sesenti, Seratus Tahun
tracks.subject: a cave guide at Gua Tempurung in Perak leading a noisy school group through the limestone chambers, telling them over and over not to touch the stalactites because the oil on their hands stops the stone growing and one centimetre takes about a hundred years

tracks.title: 搖鈴仔的阿伯 Iô Lîng-á ê A-peh
tracks.mood: cheeky, skipping and proud, a whole school dancing to one old man's wrist
tracks.subject: the electric school bell at a Taiwanese primary school breaks for a week and the old school caretaker rings the periods by hand with a rusty brass handbell from the storeroom, until the pupils refuse to go in when the repaired bell returns

tracks.title: 會行路的洗衫機 Ē Kiânn-lōo ê Sé-sann-ki
tracks.mood: sunny, brassy and giddy, a bargain that dances off across the kitchen
tracks.subject: an auntie who haggles across three towns' secondhand shops for one used washing machine, gets it home for 3,500 with a free hose, and on its first spin cycle it walks across the kitchen while her husband, son and daughter chase it, until the daughter sits on it and her husband wedges a wood chip under its short leg

tracks.title: 接枝 Tsiap-ki
tracks.mood: tender, sly and patient, a husband keeping a three-year secret in a tree
tracks.subject: a husband secretly grafting Irwin (aiwen) mango scions onto the sour native mango tree his grandfather planted behind the house, because his wife buys Irwin mangoes at the market every year, and three summers later the tree fruits both kinds

tracks.title: 國民法官六號 Kok-bîn Huat-kuann La̍k-hō
tracks.subject: an ordinary man drawn by lot as citizen judge number six (Taiwan's citizen judge system) for a six-day fraud trial, who may tell no one, tells his wife it's a business trip, eats cold pork-chop lunchboxes in silence with five strangers, and casts his vote

tracks.title: 九降風的菜脯 Káu-kàng-hong ê Tshài-póo
tracks.mood: hazy, tender and windswept, a long dry winter on a rooftop
tracks.subject: a granddaughter spending one dry, windy Hsinchu winter on the rooftop with her living grandmother making sun-dried radish (菜脯): weeks of salting, turning the radish morning and night on bamboo trays in the northeast 'nine-descending' wind, while the grandmother talks about working the salt pans and the salty radish grandpa brought when he first came courting

tracks.title: ตำนี้ใครกินไหว (Who Can Eat This Somtam)
tracks.mood: rowdy, sweaty and laughing at itself
tracks.subject: a Bangkok office's Friday pot-luck where Pae from purchasing brings a somtam made with thirty bird's-eye chillies; one bite each sends the whole 14th floor queueing at the water cooler, while the narrator calmly keeps eating and becomes the only person Pae will pound it for

tracks.title: ไพ่ตองของยาย (Grandma's Tong Cards)
tracks.subject: a man spending his first Songkran at his girlfriend's family home learning her grandmother's tong card game to win the family over, losing every hand for three days, until the grandmother deals to him first and calls him หลาน

tracks.title: อ่านได้หมด (I Can Read Them All)
tracks.subject: a Roi Et rice farmer on his first trip abroad, a temple tour bus to Vientiane his daughter paid for, who bets the Lao driver a crate of Beerlao that he can read every Lao shop sign because it is nearly Isan, and loses to a French bakery sign and the railway station sign he reads as a discount on lights

tracks.title: สูบน้ำคืนเดือนสาม (Pumping Water in the Third Month)
tracks.subject: a young man running the diesel pump every dry-season night onto his family's shallot beds on the Chi river bank in Maha Sarakham, and the young woman who runs the pump on the next plot; they talk across the ditch over the engine noise until he offers to carry her pipe

tracks.title: บลูเบอร์รี่ป่า (Wild Blueberries)
tracks.mood: tired, wry and homesick but grinning
tracks.subject: a Chaiyaphum man on his third summer picking wild blueberries in the forests of Finnish Lapland, counting buckets at the scale each evening, cooking sticky rice in a borrowed school kitchen, and noticing the August sun is still up at eleven at night

tracks.title: Vạch Nước Sáu Giờ
tracks.subject: a man who rides onto Long Biên Bridge at six every morning to watch the woman he loves read the Red River water-level gauge staff below, learning the name of every painted mark until she says that is enough to meet her mother

tracks.title: Xô Thứ Một Nghìn
tracks.genre: Vietnamese experimental folk-rap with metal percussion
tracks.subject: a hired crew of four and the family alone (husband, wife, their teenage son, the wife's brother) pouring their Hanoi house's concrete roof slab in one morning by bucket chain, the wife's mother on a plastic stool writing down whoever passes slowly, and the eight of them sitting on the still-wet roof when she finally opens the beer

tracks.title: Diều Đê Ngõ Chợ
tracks.subject: kids of one Hanoi alley off the Yên Phụ dike road hauling every kite they own up onto the dike on one windy dry-season afternoon, trying to keep as many in the air at once as they can, until their strings tangle with the kites from the next alley and both gangs end up on the slope unknotting them together (not a formal contest)

tracks.title: Rồi Răng Nữa?
tracks.subject: an old woman in a Huế garden house reading aloud on the porch the letters from her late-life pen-friend, a retired teacher in Quy Nhơn she met through a newspaper column, while her husband pretends to read the paper and keeps asking 'rồi răng nữa?'

tracks.title: Đếm Mạ Bằng Tiếng Tây Ban Nha
tracks.subject: a Vietnamese rice engineer on a cooperation project in Los Palacios, Cuba, who counts seedlings wrong in Spanish all afternoon beside the Cuban agronomist Yanelis, teaches her to ask 'ăn cơm chưa', and files for an extension after three harvests

tracks.title: 唔該唔好掂
tracks.subject: a gallery attendant at the Hong Kong Museum of History who spends her whole shift telling visitors not to touch the red-sail fishing junk and the old tram, a schoolboy who climbs in and rings the tram bell, and her own secret tap on the junk's glass case after closing

tracks.title: 三點四十五
tracks.subject: a married couple who both work non-teaching jobs at the same secondary school, the lab technician and the librarian, meeting every day at 3:45 after the bell to split one cold bottle of Vitasoy in the empty science prep room, six years on

tracks.title: 七點半校門口
tracks.subject: a young woman whose older sister paid her HK$8,000 school fees and would not take an IOU; with no money to repay, she walks her six-year-old niece to school at 7:30 every weekday for a year, ticking each trip on a fridge calendar, and when she finally brings the HK$8,000 the sister pushes it back and says the school runs aren't finished

tracks.title: 邊個又郁咗
tracks.subject: a man who spends a Sunday putting the family's living-room TV channels in a sensible order, then wages a running war with his mum, little sister, grandpa and dad, who keep scrambling it, until a family vote puts the Korean drama channel first

tracks.title: 數錯湯圓
tracks.subject: an old man in Tsuen Wan who, every winter solstice eve, hand-rolls black-sesame tong yuen, two each, for his three grown children's households and grandkids coming for dinner, keeps miscounting, ends up three over, then needs four more when his son brings his girlfriend's mother and his son-in-law wants four, and gives his own bowl to his grandson

tracks.title: 臭花倒數
tracks.subject: Taipei botanical garden staff and a growing crowd waiting four nights for a giant corpse flower (titan arum) to open, everyone holding their noses and refusing to go home

tracks.title: 阿姨的手不要抖
tracks.subject: a high-school boy who tries every trick for a month (compliments, a birthday card, helping wipe trays) to stop the canteen auntie's ladle shaking the braised pork back into the pot

tracks.title: 原封不動
tracks.mood: giddy, sly, in on the joke
tracks.subject: an office secret-santa exchange on the last Friday before Christmas where, gift by gift, it emerges that everyone has quietly regifted last year's present, still in its wrapping

tracks.title: 雙人車 一個人騎
tracks.subject: a woman at a riverside bike-rental shop counter ending the annual tandem-bicycle rental her ex signed them both up for, while the owner keeps asking where the other rider is; she takes the tandem out alone for one last lap along the river before handing it back

tracks.title: 四個月見一次針頭
tracks.subject: a couple who first met in the next beds at a blood donation centre and have gone back together every four months for six years, he still scared of the needle and holding her hand, she squeezing the rubber ball for him

tracks.title: Send It to the Lab
tracks.mood: swaggering, sheepish and laughing at himself
tracks.subject: a first-year hobby farmer in Ohio who mails a zip bag of his back-field dirt to the state university extension lab, brags to the feed store all month, and gets the report back saying it is mostly gravel and needs two tons of lime

tracks.title: Through the Studio Glass
tracks.subject: a night security guard at a city art museum who falls for the paintings conservator working late on cleaning old varnish off a harbour painting, watching her through the conservation studio glass on every round and bringing her a vending-machine tea at three

tracks.title: One Question at Window Nine
tracks.subject: a man queueing at seven in the morning outside the US embassy in London for his work visa interview, paying a shop round the corner five pounds to hold his phone, rehearsing answers for an hour, and getting asked one question at window nine

tracks.title: Six Hundred Grams
tracks.subject: a hedgehog rescue volunteer in a Sheffield terrace weighing autumn hoglets on kitchen scales at two in the morning, feeding them cat biscuits until each one passes six hundred grams and can be released before hibernation

tracks.title: Grandad Nicked It from Kew
tracks.subject: a Peckham man carrying a six-foot cheese plant in a Lidl bag-for-life to Kew Gardens across London by bus, because his grandad pinched it as a finger-long cutting from the Palm House in 1971 and it has since eaten the whole front room, and the Kew botanist who looks at the leaves, says they lost that exact one in a 1987 storm, and takes it back for the glasshouse with his grandad's name on the label

tracks.title: Lampu Buah Naga
tracks.subject: a Banyuwangi dragon-fruit farmer who lights his field with yellow lamps from six till five to force off-season flowers, watches his electricity bill double, and ends up charging the courting teenagers who sneak in at night five thousand rupiah to take photos among the glowing poles

tracks.title: Gosok Bak Minum Dulu
tracks.subject: a Komodo keeper at Surabaya Zoo and the man who signs up as a Sunday volunteer because of her; she makes him scrub the water trough every Sunday for a month before she lets him hold the feeding pole

tracks.title: Laporan Jam Dua Pagi
tracks.subject: the night observer at the Merapi observation post in Kaliurang alone with the seismograph, counting avalanche quakes and phoning in the alert-level report to Yogyakarta, staged by himself as a one-man opera

tracks.title: Kantor Pos Taichung
tracks.subject: an Indonesian caregiver in Taichung spending her one Sunday off at the post office, where the parcel home to Cilacap is half a kilo over and she takes out her own new sandals so her son's school shoes still fit in the box

tracks.title: Motif Jengkol
tracks.genre: Indonesian late-60s beat pop (Koes Plus style)
tracks.subject: a cap stamper at a batik workshop in Pekalongan who presses the hot copper stamp four hundred times a day, ordered by the owner's wife to stamp her new design, a jengkol-bean motif, onto three hundred metres of cloth, which the town hall then picks as the Friday uniform, so the whole town wears his stinky-bean batik and he walks around deadpan proud

tracks.title: 二割まで
tracks.subject: a man whose dropped wallet comes back from the Tokyo police lost-property centre with every last coin, agonising by the phone over whether to give the high-school baseball player who found it five percent or the full twenty percent reward

tracks.title: 雪の大谷攻城戦
tracks.subject: an April snow-clearing crew on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route cutting the 20-metre 'snow corridor' at Murodo open with a rotary snow plough, the foreman directing it like a castle siege, the bus road due to open to tourists in a week

tracks.title: 赤で「残す」
tracks.genre: Japanese a cappella vocal group pop
tracks.subject: a junior editor at a dictionary publisher who falls for the proofreader across the desk island; during the revision he slips a new example sentence for 恋 into the draft, and the galley comes back with her red-pen mark: 残す

tracks.title: 橋をたたく
tracks.subject: an expressway bridge inspector who closes one lane at ten at night and works under the deck until dawn, tapping the concrete with a hammer and circling every spot that sounds hollow in chalk

tracks.title: 日曜は二百メートル
tracks.subject: a man walking his twenty-two-year-old, thirty-kilo spurred tortoise along the riverbank every Sunday morning, two hundred metres an hour with dandelion stops, and carrying him home in his arms

tracks.title: 허물 수집가
tracks.subject: a seven-year-old collecting cicada shells off the zelkova trees of her apartment-complex playground in August, hiding them in egg cartons at the bottom of the fridge to reach one hundred before school starts

tracks.title: 삼삼 활주로
tracks.subject: the Incheon Airport wildlife-control team at dawn, driving the runway in hi-vis vests, firing blank cartridges and playing recorded hawk calls to clear a flock of egrets off runway 33 before the 6:10 first landing

tracks.title: 거꾸로 새긴 이름
tracks.subject: a dojang seal-engraver in a second-floor Insadong workshop carving forty name seals in one day for a company's new hires, who start the next morning, reading every name backwards as he cuts it in mirror image

tracks.title: 일곱 분마다
tracks.subject: a man staying up through the thirty-hour wood firing of his potter girlfriend's climbing kiln in Icheon, feeding it two logs every seven minutes beside her, with a ring box in his bag he plans to give her the day the kiln is opened

tracks.title: 녹아라 계량기
tracks.subject: a young man in a one-room flat at 6:40 on the third morning of a cold-wave warning, with a job interview at 9:30, thawing the frozen water meter by the front door with microwaved bottled water and a hairdryer while the landlord lectures him by phone

tracks.title: Ayam Abang, Cili Saya
tracks.genre: Malay folk-tune modern pop (pop moden bernuansa tradisional)
tracks.subject: a wife whose twelve new chilli plants by the back fence are dug up every day by her husband's three free-range kampung hens, until he offers her one warm egg a day as rent for the garden

tracks.title: Van Buku Khamis Kedua
tracks.subject: a man courting the librarian on the state mobile-library van that parks under the balai raya's angsana tree in his kampung every second Thursday evening, borrowing thick books he never opens (tractor manuals, a Russian novel, a cookbook in French) just to have a reason to come back and return them, until she stamps a return date that falls on a Saturday and writes her own name beside it

tracks.title: Ular Dalam Bonet
tracks.subject: a Bomba snake-catching unit pulling a 4-metre python out of the engine bay of a Proton Saga in a Shah Alam shopping-mall car park while the owner livestreams the whole thing, begging viewers for likes and asking the firemen to wave

tracks.title: Gendang Di Pagar Sekolah
tracks.subject: the security guard of a kampung primary school who brings his gendang to the gate on the first day of term, with the bus driver on serunai and the office clerk on gong, until the crying Year One children march in and the mothers are the ones crying

tracks.title: Kanan Ke Kiri
tracks.subject: a signboard painter with thirty years of steady hands who cannot read Jawi, joining a Tuesday-night adult Jawi class in the community hall so he can repaint the cloth shop's sign without getting a single letter backwards

tracks.title: 我毋是鮭魚 Guá M̄-sī Kue-hî
tracks.mood: deadpan, sheepish and bouncy, a joke the singer has finally stopped living inside
tracks.subject: a man who changed his legal name to 'Lim Salmon' in 2021 for a free sushi-restaurant feast and has lived with it on every bank queue screen and job interview since, back at the household registration office for his third and, by law, last name change, while the clerk reminds him this one is final

tracks.title: 四點落梨山 Sì Tiám Lo̍h Lî-san
tracks.mood: giddy, wide awake and racing the clock, a mountain descent against the auction bell
tracks.subject: a young woman who takes over her father's cabbage truck the night his back gives out, loads four hundred crates of high-mountain cabbage in Lishan at three in the morning and races down the switchbacks through Yilan at first light to make the seven o'clock auction at the Taipei fruit and vegetable wholesale market, her mother phoning every hour and one cabbage bouncing off the back on a bend

tracks.title: 菜寮溪 Tshài-liâu-khe
tracks.mood: sunny, stubborn and warm-hearted, an old man's small triumph
tracks.subject: a retired farmer in Zuojhen, Tainan, who walks the dry white riverbed of the Tsailiao Creek every winter with a small hammer looking for fossils, is called mad by the village until the young woman at the local fossil museum identifies his find as a rhinoceros tooth and writes his name under it, and now leads a line of children with toy hammers

tracks.title: 通譯 Thong-i̍k
tracks.mood: tense, dry and wry, with a soft landing
tracks.subject: a young Taigi interpreter at a district court civil hearing, translating for an old farmer who speaks only Taigi against a construction company whose new wall sits thirty centimetres inside his field, swallowing the curse he shouts at the company's lawyer, and hearing the judge order a fresh survey

tracks.title: 蜂仔佮龍眼花 Phang-á kah Lîng-gíng-hue
tracks.mood: tender, shy and warm, a sunny week of blossom season side by side
tracks.subject: a young migratory beekeeper who trucks forty hives into a Dongshan longan orchard for the April blossom and courts the owner's daughter while she walks the rows with him in the midday heat; she laughs at his veil, binds a sting on his wrist with her handkerchief, dips her finger into the first frame of longan honey before her father can, and asks him to bring the bees back next April

tracks.title: ป้ายใหม่มาแล้ว (Here Comes the New Sign)
tracks.subject: the megaphone woman on a Bang Phlat district-office crew swapping the faded blue street-name signs down one soi in a single afternoon, announcing every stop through a megaphone while the aunties argue the new sign is spelled wrong, a noodle shop owner protests the two thousand business cards he printed with the old soi number, and kids pose for photos under each sign before the paint is dry

tracks.title: เลื่อยน้ำแข็ง (Ice Saw)
tracks.subject: a night-shift worker at a Bangkok ice plant during a 43-degree April heatwave, hauling 150-kilo blocks out of the brine tanks, sawing them into quarters and loading ten trucks before dawn, the only cold man in the city

tracks.title: จิ้งหรีดไม่ยอมร้อง (Silent Crickets)
tracks.subject: a cricket farmer outside Khon Kaen whose forty concrete rings of crickets chirp all night every night, until the man from a Bangkok protein-snack company comes to inspect and every ring goes silent, until her husband plays his electric phin and they start up again

tracks.title: มุมขวาล่าง (Bottom Right Corner)
tracks.subject: a deaf sign-language teacher in Chiang Mai who watches her husband, a former student from her Saturday class at the public library, interpret the northern regional evening news in the small box in the bottom-right corner of the screen; at the end of every bulletin he touches his collar twice, their sign that he is coming home

tracks.title: ซี่ลวดสามสิบหกซี่ (Thirty-Six Spokes)
tracks.genre: J-pop piano band rock (sung in Thai)
tracks.subject: a 19-year-old apprentice at an old Bangkok bicycle-repair shop rebuilding her first customer's rusted delivery bike spoke by spoke, watched by the shop owner, before the rider comes back to collect it at six

tracks.title: Câu Thơ Trong Vành Nón
tracks.subject: a man who crosses by boat to a Huế conical-hat maker's yard, orders a nón bài thơ and asks her to hide a line of poetry between the leaf layers of the brim; when he holds it up to the sun the cut-paper line is hers, not the verses he brought

tracks.title: Lớp Sơn Thứ Mười Một
tracks.subject: an apprentice in a Hạ Thái lacquer workshop wet-sanding and re-coating the same black tray for its eleventh layer while the boss taps out the layers on the bench like a DJ counting bars

tracks.title: Gặt Cói Nga Sơn
tracks.genre: Thanh Hóa hò sông Mã folk-pop
tracks.mood: teasing, sun-baked and full of work energy
tracks.subject: a garment-factory worker home from Bắc Ninh for one week of the June sedge harvest in Nga Sơn, cutting cói with her aunt's women's team who call hò sông Mã lines to keep the sickles together and tease her blistered city hands until she calls a line back

tracks.title: Bướm Đêm Tên Lớp Mình
tracks.subject: a Hanoi biology student on a summer moth survey in Hoàng Liên National Park who hangs a white sheet under a lamp every night, logs two hundred and twelve moths, and names the unidentified ones after her classmates in the class group chat, until her lecturer says the one named after Ngân may be a new species

tracks.title: Ba Trăm Mét Trước Bình Minh
tracks.subject: a Hanoi tree crew moving a century-old banyan overnight for a road widening, wrapping the root ball in burlap and wire and inching it 300 metres on a low trailer to its new pit before the first morning traffic

tracks.title: 大帽山結霜啦
tracks.subject: the January night Hong Kong chased frost up Tai Mo Shan: minibus queues stretching down the street outside Tsuen Wan station, crowds walking the last half of the road wrapped in bedsheets, a stranger pouring hot tea from a flask, and a secondary-school boy at the summit filming ice growing along a fence wire while everyone around him goes quiet

tracks.title: 淋水嗰個
tracks.subject: a couple renting a hundred-square-foot plot at a weekend leisure farm in Kam Tin for a year, where she does the watering and he picks off the caterpillars and snails, and in August he leaves the first red tomato for her to pick

tracks.title: 開鎖佬
tracks.subject: a 24-hour locksmith in Kwun Tong on one night's calls: he refuses to open the door for a drunk young man whose girlfriend has locked him out, frees an old woman's cat that shut itself in her bathroom, and at dawn finds he has lost his own keys and has to call his apprentice, who charges him the full fee

tracks.title: 花生有人要咗
tracks.mood: bittersweet, earnest, glad and a little lost
tracks.subject: an office worker who has walked the same nine-year-old black shelter dog, Peanut, every Saturday for two years at a dog shelter in Sheung Shui, and arrives one Saturday to find her kennel empty because a family adopted her on Wednesday, so he walks a young brown dog called Tofu instead

tracks.title: 牛呀牛讓一讓
tracks.subject: a Lantau cattle volunteer at eight on a weekday morning on South Lantau Road, coaxing a dozen feral cattle off the white line with a flag and a whistle while three buses, a lorry and a taxi wait; the lead cow Ah Fa chews slowly at her before moving, a new calf hesitates beside its mother, and the first bus driver leans out to promise her a bun tomorrow

tracks.title: 借過借過
tracks.subject: an overnight porter at a taichung hospital pushing beds, wheelchairs and specimen boxes twenty thousand steps a night, shouting 'excuse me' at every corner, and the grandmother on her way to a two a.m. x-ray who tells him to push faster

tracks.title: 四十隻小羊
tracks.subject: a helper on a taitung dairy-goat farm in kidding season bottle-feeding forty kids at five in the morning, every one named after a colleague from his old office, and the bossy one named after his manager who keeps eating his straw hat

tracks.title: 替你繫的那一隻
tracks.subject: two volunteers at a dawn bird-ringing station on the Guandu wetland in autumn migration, weighing warblers in cloth bags; she fits the rings, he keeps the logbook and writes her initial beside every bird she rings, and on the last morning of the season she rings one and says it is for him

tracks.title: 十一點五十的鐘聲
tracks.subject: the four-auntie kitchen team at a Tainan primary school cooking 1,200 lunches against the 11:50 bell: steamers stacked to the ceiling, ladles swinging in choreography, and one auntie shouting class numbers as the soup buckets roll out, until the bell rings and she finally sits down with her own bowl

tracks.title: 看鏡頭
tracks.subject: an immigration officer at counter four in taoyuan airport arrivals on the three-to-six a.m. shift, repeating 'look at the camera, left index finger, right index finger, next' to three hundred passengers off a bangkok red-eye, a man with his shoes on the wrong feet, a suitcase of dried mango, and a child making a peace sign at the camera

tracks.title: King Conker
tracks.subject: a primary-school caretaker who spends September soaking and baking conkers from the playground horse chestnut, is handed a conker from the organisers' bucket at the World Conker Championships in Southwick, wins round one and loses round two to a girl from his own school

tracks.title: Touch-Move
tracks.subject: a fifteen-year-old at an under-sixteens rapidplay chess tournament in a Croydon school sports hall who trash-talks only in his head because talking at the board is banned, hangs his queen and still wins on time

tracks.title: Call the Fridgie
tracks.subject: a female refrigeration mechanic in western Sydney fixing the coolrooms of four pubs and clubs on a 46-degree day in Penrith before the Friday rush

tracks.title: Mile Nineteen
tracks.subject: a London Marathon volunteer handing out water at the mile-nineteen station at Canary Wharf, shouting the names written on runners' vests until the last walker comes through

tracks.title: I'll Write It Down
tracks.subject: a husband of twenty-two years who drives his amateur-astronomer wife to Borrego Springs every August for the Perseids and writes down every meteor she calls out, though he never sees one himself

tracks.title: Tempa Lagi
tracks.subject: the youngest of five hammermen in a gong smithy in Wirun, Sukoharjo, forging a ninety-centimetre bronze gong ageng for a Solo dance school over three weeks of charcoal fire and hand hammers, under old Pak Darmo, who grips the red-hot disc in long tongs and keeps saying it will not sing yet, until the morning he strikes it once and sits down while the hum fills the shed

tracks.title: Regu Kancil
tracks.mood: bouncy, proud and a little cheeky
tracks.subject: a ten-year-old in scout troop Regu Kancil at his first Saturday-Sunday school scout camp, where the tent collapses before dark, the girls' troop next door mocks it, the instant noodles burn in the mess tin and his troop still wins the whistle morse-code game, whose message turns out to be 'take a bath'

tracks.title: Kartu Pos dari Tampere
tracks.mood: shy, sweet and a little comic
tracks.subject: a young Pos Indonesia courier in Malang who delivers Postcrossing postcards from Finland, Taiwan, Belarus and Germany to the same woman every Tuesday, reads them at the red light, and finally buys a card at his own post office counter to invite her for coffee, which he then has to deliver himself

tracks.title: Lima Sembilan
tracks.subject: a woman ham-radio operator on her Bekasi rooftop through the forty-eight-hour CQ World Wide contest, logging stations from Osaka to Rio and Alaska and giving every one of them the same 'five-nine' signal report, while her husband, who grumbles about the cracked roof tiles, brings up her rice and then spends the night replacing those tiles by torchlight under her antenna

tracks.title: Lutut Kanan
tracks.subject: a forty-one-year-old former second-division striker nicknamed Si Kijang, hired for three hundred thousand rupiah a match to play for a village team in an inter-kampung tarkam tournament on a harvested rice field, his right knee strapped, kicked by nineteen-year-old defenders, until the ball bounces off the bad knee into the net

tracks.title: 放水始め
tracks.mood: sweaty, heroic and a little ridiculous
tracks.subject: a bicycle-shop owner in his town's volunteer fire brigade, drilling every July night behind the community hall under a captain with a stopwatch for the prefectural fire-pump drill competition, where a twisted hose costs them points and they finish ninth

tracks.title: 全員上がって
tracks.subject: a university student working as a municipal-pool lifeguard in a 38-degree heatwave, booed by the whole pool every time he blows the whistle for the hourly ten-minute break and cheered when he lets them back in

tracks.title: 鳴らしてみてよ
tracks.subject: a flamenco guitarist who plays Friday nights at a small Spanish restaurant, finally handed the cypress guitar that the quiet luthier at the end of the counter spent two winters building, sized to her hands and with her name on the label inside

tracks.title: 笑われたら勝ち
tracks.subject: an apprentice chindon-ya in white face paint carrying the drum rig at her first All-Japan Chindon Contest in Toyama, botching her pitch for the July baseball All-Star Game so badly the crowd roars, and being told she will do the patter from tomorrow

tracks.title: ただのカード
tracks.subject: a retired man who rides one-car local trains on summer weekdays to small-town city halls to collect the free municipal manhole cards, the only adult in a queue of children on summer holiday at the sewerage counter, until a clerk runs out in her sandals to show him the real painted cover on the crossing outside

tracks.title: 맨손잡기
tracks.subject: two friends in shorts and festival T-shirts at the Hwacheon trout festival in January, betting dakgalbi on who can catch a trout bare-handed in the freezing pool and stuff it down her shirt before the whistle

tracks.title: 뒤집기
tracks.subject: a small woman in the amateur women's ssireum bout at a Dano fair, facing the butcher who has carried off the twenty-kilogram sack of rice three years running, losing the first round to a belly lift and winning the third with a turning throw

tracks.title: 조금 더 넓게
tracks.mood: warm, unhurried and quietly in love
tracks.subject: a couple on a weekend joinery course at a Seongsu-dong workshop building one two-seat wooden bench with mortise-and-tenon joints and no nails, each of them secretly moving the pencil line so the other person's half of the seat is a little wider, until the instructor asks why there are two lines in the middle

tracks.title: 마지막으로
tracks.subject: a three-member high-school heavy-metal club that rehearses behind the chemistry lab and gets seven minutes at the school festival right after the principal's speech, which runs twenty minutes over until they are left with four

tracks.title: 가 옆에 뷁
tracks.subject: a Hangul type designer drawing all 11,172 syllable blocks for a new typeface, two hundred a night at a desk in Mangwon-dong, Mapo, making sure 뷁 stands exactly as tall as 가 though nobody will ever notice

tracks.title: Ayah Paling Sado
tracks.subject: a 54-year-old school gardener from Alor Setar in the over-50 masters category of the Kedah state bodybuilding championship, spray-tanned the colour of teh tarik by his wife backstage, his children holding up a banner reading 'Ayah Paling Sado', placing third out of three entrants and lifting the trophy anyway

tracks.title: Seberang Papan
tracks.subject: a wife and husband married thirty-eight years, partners in the veterans' mixed-doubles carrom final at an Ipoh community hall, sitting across the board from each other as doubles partners must, where she reads his raised eyebrow before every flick, the opposing pair whispers that they must have secret signals, and on the last board she pots the red queen and covers it on his nod

tracks.title: Main Je, Uncle
tracks.subject: a woman piano tuner in Kuala Lumpur called to an old hotel on Jalan Raja Laut whose lobby grand has not been tuned in seven years, who sits on the lobby sofa the evening before and hears the one thing wrong with it: Uncle Stanley, the lobby pianist, has been playing every song around a dead F sharp for seven years; she fits a new string, raises the pitch in two passes, and the next evening waits for his hand to land on the note

tracks.title: Kira Kepala, Faiz!
tracks.genre: Malay musical-theatre showtune (teater muzikal ensemble number)
tracks.subject: a young Malaysian tour guide counting heads on the Great Wall at Badaling on a packed October holiday-week day, with twenty-eight mak ciks from Tanjung Karang in matching purple tudung, one pulled into a Henan family's holiday photos, one reaching the North Eighth Tower alone ahead of everyone, one demanding her climbing certificate say 'srikandi' instead of 'hero', and the count always one short

tracks.title: Bawah Sepuluh
tracks.subject: a seventeen-year-old at a WCA Rubik's cube competition in a Subang Jaya school hall chasing his first sub-ten-second average of five, one solve lost when the cube pops a piece under a chair, the boy beside him explaining that the best and worst times get dropped

tracks.title: 掠蛇阿傑 Lia̍h-tsuâ A-kia̍t
tracks.mood: swaggering, deadpan and proud of a small-town legend
tracks.subject: the ballad of A-kiat, a 23-year-old rookie at a rural Pingtung fire station whose calls are never fires: a hornet nest at the school gate, a cat stuck up a betel palm, then a two-metre cobra coiled on the uncle's leather shoes in an auntie's shoe cabinet, which he takes with tongs and a cloth sack and lets go at the foot of Mount Dawu, until the whole township calls him the Snake King

tracks.title: 我佇下跤 Guá Tī Ē-kha
tracks.subject: a couple at a Kaohsiung indoor climbing gym on a Saturday afternoon, her first time on a rope: he ties her figure-eight knot and checks it three times, belays her up the red route, and when her foot slips halfway and she hangs in midair hugging the wall he talks her into sitting back on the rope; then they swap, he falls and his extra thirty kilos yank her off the floor so they both hang there laughing, and on her last try she slaps the top hold and turns to find him still watching her from below

tracks.title: 雞寮半暝 Ke-liâu Puànn-mê
tracks.mood: sweaty, rowdy and racing the clock
tracks.subject: a Yunlin chicken-catching crew (掠雞班) of seven racing to load 400 crates from a 6,000-bird broiler house before driver A-tsai's lorry has to leave at five for its slaughterhouse slot, while foreman A-gi stands on the lorry roof with his torch and calls every crate like a variety-show emcee, bringing on Auntie Tsu with four birds a hand without looking and the Su brothers stacking crates eight high as A-tsai checks his watch and honks; with fifty crates and ten minutes to go A-gi jumps down to catch too, and the 400th crate goes up on time while the rooster in the next village is only just crowing

tracks.title: 算鳥 Sǹg Tsiáu
tracks.subject: a volunteer on the January black-faced spoonbill census at a Tainan fish-pond roost at half past five, counting sleeping birds through a scope in the north wind while a retired teacher clicks the tally counter, losing the count at 240 when a kite circles and the whole flock lifts, and starting again to find twenty more than last year

tracks.title: 削球 Siah-kiû
tracks.mood: breathless, cocky and laughing at himself
tracks.subject: a young line worker at a Taichung bicycle factory who loses every lunch-hour table-tennis game beside the forklifts to Uncle Hok, a 61-year-old forklift driver who holds his bat like a pen and chops everything back without moving his feet, with the workers betting their Yakult, until at five to one he wins a single game 11-9 and Uncle Hok says tomorrow he'll try

tracks.title: ฉายให้เธอคนเดียว (A Show for One)
tracks.subject: a husband and wife who have run the last single-screen cinema in Lampang for forty years, he threading the 35mm projectors upstairs and she selling tickets downstairs; on closing night he borrows a print of the film that was showing the night he first saw her from the Thai Film Archive and screens it for her alone in row F, deliberately missing the last reel changeover as he did in 1985 when he was watching her instead of the cue marks

tracks.title: ไดโนเสาร์คอยาว (The Long-Neck Dinosaur)
tracks.subject: a kindergarten class trip to the Sirindhorn Dinosaur Museum in Kalasin, where the children count the neck vertebrae of the long-neck sauropod skeleton out loud and keep losing count, a boy named Ton Kla insists a fossil egg in the glass case is his and wants to take it home to hatch, and the teacher hides behind the T-rex model and roars

tracks.title: ลงตมนำกัน (Mud For Two)
tracks.subject: the builder on his village's team at the Yasothon rocket festival, whose bamboo rocket hisses and sits on the launch ramp, and the girl from the rival team who claims the right to throw him into the mud pit herself, then jumps in after him before her own team's rocket is lit

tracks.title: สามหมื่นเมตร (Thirty Thousand Metres)
tracks.subject: a Mathayom 5 girl in a provincial school science club who spent a year's lunch money on a weather balloon carrying a small camera, sitting on the school football field the night before the launch and wanting to see her own town from thirty kilometres up

tracks.title: เทริดคือหมวกกันน็อก (My Crown's My Helmet)
tracks.subject: a Nora dancer hired by the provincial transport office to perform helmet verses at Phatthalung schools, who tells six hundred students his beaded crown is his helmet, then sees the headmaster ride off bareheaded and improvises a verse about him over the school loudspeakers

tracks.title: Phun Muỗi Tới Rồi
tracks.subject: the smallest nurse on a Saigon ward health station's dengue-fogging crew, carrying the twelve-kilogram fogger on her shoulder through the alleys one Saturday after three dengue cases in alley 187: kids count her in as she pulls the starter and chase the white smoke, aunties slam their doors until they see larvae swimming in the water bowls under their own cabinet legs, and the crew clears the last alley just before the evening rush

tracks.title: Dế Mèn Quá Hạn
tracks.subject: a Hanoi district librarian retiring on Friday who tracks down the boy who borrowed Dế Mèn phiêu lưu ký in 2014, works out his fine to the đồng including leap years, finds him at the fire station reading it to his crew on night shifts, stamps it returned and lends it to him again as her last loan

tracks.title: Anh Ơi, Tuyết Nè
tracks.subject: a Saigon couple who saved one 500,000-đồng note a month for five years for their first trip abroad, seeing snow for the first time in Sapporo and building a cup-sized snowman on the hotel windowsill with a convenience-store mandarin for a nose

tracks.title: Giọng Vịt Đực
tracks.subject: the only boy in a Phú Thọ lower-secondary school's hát Xoan club, made to hold the drum and lead the giáo trống call as the kép opposite twelve girl đào, whose voice starts breaking in February and squawks like a drake on the high note at every rehearsal; at the Hùng Kings' anniversary performance in the village đình it cracks again in front of the whole village, the twelve đào drown it out in unison, the front-row children quack along all evening and the village head asks him to keep the duck next year

tracks.title: Oxyz, Tha Cho Tao
tracks.subject: a Year-12 student in the last fifteen minutes of the national graduation exam's ninety-minute maths paper on a 39-degree June afternoon, three Oxyz geometry questions blank, a snapped 2B pencil and the invigilator's footsteps coming down the aisle

tracks.title: 行頭排
tracks.subject: a 42-year-old office worker who last played trombone in his school band in 1999, roped in by his niece, drum major of a Tuen Mun youth marching band, when the band's only trombonist flies to Osaka for Lunar New Year; marching in the front row of the Lunar New Year night parade in Tsim Sha Tsui he misses her whistle to halt, plays on alone into a squad of American cheerleaders, and ducks to the roadside until his band's bass drum catches up

tracks.title: 六件蛋撻
tracks.subject: six office friends dressed as a box of egg tarts in the South Stand at the first Hong Kong Sevens at Kai Tak, dancing all weekend and missing every try, including the one in the final

tracks.title: 寫咗先望
tracks.subject: a shy man who sings the scholar's part in a Saturday amateur Cantonese-opera singing club in a To Kwa Wan community hall, paired for the annual show in a duet with the woman who joined in March, who only looks at her where the teacher has pencilled the word 'look' into his score, until on show night he opens it at the music stand and finds she has pencilled one beside every line

tracks.title: 四個一齊到
tracks.mood: grinding, stubborn, sweaty and a bit absurd
tracks.subject: four office colleagues doing the Oxfam Trailwalker, 100 km of the MacLehose Trail in under 48 hours where all four must cross the line together, and the one who sits down on the Lion Rock steps at 3 a.m. to quit

tracks.title: 第四隻東風
tracks.subject: one of the last hand-carvers of mahjong tiles, in a narrow Jordan shopfront, spending three afternoons carving a single East Wind to replace the one a Yau Ma Tei table has gone without for years in a forty-year-old set his own master carved, copying the master's long-tailed stroke from the three surviving East tiles and steeping the too-white blank in pu'er until its yellow matches by eye in the doorway's afternoon sun

tracks.title: 甩繩的人
tracks.subject: the rope-turner on a junior-high double-dutch team at the county championship who has turned the ropes for three years without ever jumping, until the coach swaps her in for the last freestyle routine and her best friend turns for her

tracks.title: 冰磚來了
tracks.subject: a zookeeper in a thirty-seven-degree July heatwave wheeling out frozen blocks of watermelon, apples and a whole chicken for the sun bear, the orangutans and the tiger, while sweating visitors fan themselves with zoo maps and an old man in a straw hat asks to buy one

tracks.title: 多一顆
tracks.subject: a planetarium show narrator whose girlfriend buys a ticket for the last Wednesday show every week, always sits in row G seat 7 and coughs in the dark whenever he skips a line of the summer-sky script; on her thirteenth visit, the last Wednesday of the summer season, he adds a line of his own mid-show, telling the full dome that tonight's summer triangle has one extra star, sitting in G7

tracks.title: 踢給你看
tracks.subject: a sophomore girl in a university taekwondo club at the September club fair, losing the sign-up race to the judo club's booth next door, where the club with fewer names on its sheet at five o'clock gives up the Wednesday-night slot in the shared basement dojo, until she calls the hundred-kilo judo captain over to hold a board at head height, clips his thumb with the first spinning back kick, splits the board with the second, and wins forty-one to forty, the last name on her sheet being his

tracks.title: 十二公分
tracks.subject: a weather observer halfway through his shift at the Yushan North Peak weather station, measuring the winter's first snow with a ruler at five in the morning, reading the numbers down to the base over the radio, and losing his biscuits to a yellow-throated marten

tracks.title: Ring-Pull
tracks.subject: a man combing Tynemouth Longsands with a borrowed metal detector for the wedding ring he lost swimming, while his wife on the steps offers to marry him again with a ring-pull

tracks.title: Under-Nines
tracks.subject: a fourteen-year-old referee at a Sunday-morning under-nines football match on pitch three, shouted at by touchline dads in a league that keeps no score

tracks.title: Somebody Press The Button
tracks.subject: a council events officer whose booked soap-opera vet cancels at four o'clock on the night of the town's Christmas lights switch-on, until a fourteen-year-old Labrador presses the button

tracks.title: Up To My Shoulder
tracks.subject: a Mississippi Delta man noodling for a flathead catfish under a cypress log in the Sunflower River with his bare arm, and the forty-one-pound fish that bites back

tracks.title: Old Sober
tracks.subject: a yakamein seller pushing two coolers on a grocery cart four miles behind a Sunday second-line parade in New Orleans, selling old sober at every stop

tracks.title: Kaos Keramat
tracks.subject: a Persib supporter in Bandung who has not washed his knock-off blue jersey through nine unbeaten home games, while his boarding-house mates leave cream detergent outside his door

tracks.title: Padel Jam Enam
tracks.subject: four girlfriends on a six a.m. padel court in South Jakarta, three of them there for the photos and the narrator there to win

tracks.title: Dadak Merak
tracks.subject: a young pembarong in Ponorogo training to hold the fifty-kilogram dadak merak peacock mask by his teeth, three weeks before the Grebeg Suro festival

tracks.title: Bas deng Melodi
tracks.subject: a married couple in a Tomohon church kolintang group, she on the melody bars at one end of the row and he on the bass box at the other, cueing each other across the hall at Thursday rehearsals

tracks.title: Sarapan di Bibir Kawah
tracks.subject: a Rinjani porter from Sembalun cooking banana pancakes on the crater rim at dawn while his trekkers go up to the summit

tracks.title: 君の天気予報
tracks.subject: a man who watches his girlfriend present the local evening weather forecast every night and leaves his umbrella at home whenever she says it will be fine, even after she got it wrong and he came home soaked

tracks.title: 行かないで焼き芋屋さん
tracks.subject: running out in sandals on a winter Friday night after the stone-baked sweet-potato truck's loudspeaker call and finally catching it at the shrine slope for the last 800-yen potato

tracks.title: 一音目で払ってやる
tracks.subject: a first-year in a high-school competitive karuta club at the July tournament at Ōmi Jingū, sweeping cards across the tatami before the reader finishes the first syllable, against a smug third-year from a rival school who sneered at her

tracks.title: 片耳のトラ
tracks.subject: a one-eared ginger stray who rules a shopping street meeting a fluffy white house cat on a pink harness outside the croquette shop, and hiding behind the shop girl's legs

tracks.title: シナノキの六月
tracks.subject: an urban beekeeper who keeps hives on the roof of a Ginza department store, lifting the frames at noon above the lunchtime crowds and tasting the honey turn minty when the street's linden trees flower in June

tracks.title: 영차 영차
tracks.subject: a white campus food-delivery robot, unit three, that gets stuck on the same five-centimetre kerb outside the engineering building every lunchtime, and the students in department jackets who form a chanting cheer squad to lift its front wheels and push it over while the spicy pork rice bowls are still warm

tracks.title: 왼쪽 굽
tracks.genre: Korean boom bap with psych-rock guitar
tracks.subject: the old man in the shoe-repair booth at a subway exit who reads a young job-seeker's habits from his worn left heel while re-heeling his only dress shoes the night before an interview

tracks.title: 정오의 갈매기
tracks.subject: a stand-off on an island car-ferry deck at noon between a woman holding one bag of shrimp crackers and a seagull standing on one leg on the rail, which wins the last cracker when she only pretends to throw it

tracks.title: 숯가마
tracks.subject: a whole Sunday lost in a jjimjilbang, going back and forth between the eighty-degree charcoal kiln room and the ice room until the wall clock and the TV reruns stop making sense

tracks.title: 제일 단 거
tracks.subject: two seasonal tangerine pickers on a Seogwipo farm in December who fall for each other; she peels one tangerine from every tenth crate behind the owner's back and splits it with him, always handing over the sweeter half

tracks.title: Tuala Merah
tracks.mood: tender, proud and a little lovesick
